sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: Accepted. The candidate is semantically faithful: it targets ships, preserves the applicability conditions and metric-tonne quantity structure, uses the required canonical terms and datatypes, and correctly reports violations when either protection status is missing an exactly typed boolean true or contains any non-true value, including coexistence of true and false values.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Repair both violation queries so each required protection status is exactly true, not merely present among values: reject any applicable ship having a status value other than true (or constrain each status property with sh:hasValue true and appropriate cardinality). The current FILTER NOT EXISTS pattern passes when true and false values coexist, creating accidental pass logic. Preserve the existing ship target, applicability conditions, thresholds, datatypes, and metric unit.

The SPARQL constraint has inverted SHACL violation logic: it selects applicable ships whose two statuses are true and have no non-true values, so compliant data is reported as a violation while missing/false statuses can pass. Rewrite the constraint to select applicable ships when either status lacks an exactly typed xsd:boolean true value or has any value other than exactly true; ensure coexistence of true and false is rejected. Preserve the prior instruction and applicability thresholds, datatypes, and metric unit. Also remove the extra `$this a nltl:oilTanker` applicability condition: the verified requirement uses the supplied shipType value equal to oil_tanker, and adding class membership can incorrectly exclude applicable ships.

Preserve the corrected violation direction and all prior applicability instructions, but make the protection-status checks reject every value that is not exactly the typed boolean true. The current `?status != "true"^^xsd:boolean` comparison can raise a type error and fail to reject an incompatible value coexisting with a true value. Replace each non-true filter with a datatype-aware condition such as `FILTER (datatype(?status) != xsd:boolean || ?status != "true"^^xsd:boolean)`, or add corresponding ship-targeted property shapes with `sh:datatype xsd:boolean` while retaining the exact-true query checks. Do not add an oilTanker class condition or alter the existing applicability, threshold, datatype, or unit requirements.

Accepted. The candidate is semantically faithful: it targets ships, preserves the applicability conditions and metric-tonne quantity structure, uses the required canonical terms and datatypes, and correctly reports violations when either protection status is missing an exactly typed boolean true or contains any non-true value, including coexistence of true and false values.
